operator_io_quirks: No declared FKs at all (all tables fks=[]), so process_order yields one level; TS will not link station.id<->status.station_id or trip.start/end_station_id<->station.id, so cross-table joins get independent random values.
status and weather have no PK; sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op there, so duplicate rows survive (status has 299936 rows, distinct station_id only 70).
status is huge (299936 rows) and trip is 658901 rows; read_schema must rowid-sample (max_rows_per_table) or the read dominates wall time; original_sizes still full count.
trip.id distinct=200000 but rows=658901 -> PK duplicates exist in the original; TS's PK dedup will shrink trip far below its chosen size.

Text-stored dates in three different formats: station.installation_date '8/6/2013' (M/D/YYYY), trip.start_date/end_date '8/29/2013 9:08' (M/D/YYYY H:MM), status.time '2013/08/29 12:12:01' (YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS), weather.date '8/29/2013'. All declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, not Date.
weather.precipitation_inches is TEXT holding numeric strings plus 'T' (trace); declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, so numeric comparisons on it are fragile.
weather.events has empty string '' and mixed case ('Rain' vs 'rain', 'Fog-Rain'); String fuzzer will emit random charset strings, not these tokens.
weather.max_wind_Speed_mph has mixed-case column name (capital S); identifier quoting must preserve original spelling.
Nulls present in many weather columns (max_gust_speed_mph 24.5%, dew/humidity 1.5%, trip.zip_code 3.1%); declared notnull=0 everywhere except station.id and trip.id.
trip.zip_code is INTEGER with nulls; weather.zip_code is TEXT with same-looking values ('94107') -> storage class contradicts across tables, join on zip_code is type-mismatched.
station.lat/long are REAL with values like 37.33/-121.90; Number fuzzer range is [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none) -> will not stay near real coordinates.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL; empty clone is just 4 CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: All TEXT columns (name, city, installation_date, start_date, end_date, time, date, events, precipitation_inches, subscription_type, zip_code in weather) get String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, so dates/times/enums become garbage -> many implausible values (FN risk on date/enum predicates).

All INTEGER/REAL columns get Number fuzzer with default scale (no type args) -> range roughly [-10^0,10^0] perturbed by +-1/+-2; lat/long, temperatures, zip codes, bike_id all collapse to tiny integers -> implausible (FN on range predicates like temperature>70, zip_code LIKE '94%').

No FKs -> fill_foreign_keys_consistently never runs; station_id/start_station_id/end_station_id are independent random ints, so joins station.id=status.station_id almost never match -> join queries return empty or tiny results (FP/FN on join cardinality).

status/weather have no PK -> no dedup; TS may emit many duplicate rows, but with random ints distinct is still high; ties for GROUP BY/COUNT DISTINCT on low-cardinality columns (subscription_type, city, events) are unlikely to reproduce original 2/5/6 distinct values.
trip.id PK dedup drops ~70% of drawn rows (200000 distinct of 658901) -> trip ends up much smaller than chosen size, skewing join sizes.
String fuzzer's int-like-string +1/-1 and % stripping won't help because date/time columns are non-numeric strings; no date template is learned (Date fuzzer never selected).
Number fuzzer list-range quirk (upper end overwritten to full-range max) means even with literal pool values like 74,78 the fresh draws dominate -> temperatures/zip codes drift to small ints.
Empty-string and 'T' in precipitation_inches/events are not reproduced by String fuzzer (random charset rarely yields '' or 'T') -> equality predicates on these miss.
Mixed-case column max_wind_Speed_mph: if quoting is wrong, inserts/queries fail; TS upstream upper-cases columns so it may still work, but our original-spelling path must quote.
zip_code type mismatch (INTEGER in trip, TEXT in weather) means a join trip.zip_code=weather.zip_code compares int to text -> sqlite affinity may coerce, but random values won't match anyway.

Overall: TS will produce syntactically valid but semantically implausible instances; known misses are FN from garbage dates/enums/ranges and FP from missing join ties and missing low-cardinality duplicates.
